hits.text:
🚨🚨🚨The more Franklin Templeton talks about this, the more bullish I get on $XRP, stellar:native, and hedera-hashgraph:native. 

Watch this interview.

Buckle up, this one’s gonna be a long read.

I've been following institutional blockchain adoption for years, and I genuinely believe we're watching a massive change in how the financial system manages money.

Franklin Templeton is explaining how its tokenized money-market fund can calculate interest down to the second.

An investor could hold it for just three hours and six seconds and still receive the interest earned during that exact period.

Now think about what that means for banks and asset managers handling hundreds of millions of dollars every day.

At a hypothetical 4% annual yield, $100 million earns approximately $457 in one hour, $1,370 in three hours, and $10,959 in 24 hours.

That's a lot of money when you consider how much capital institutions move between investments, payments, and trading activities.

And Franklin Templeton already introduced this Intraday Yield technology through its Benji Technology Platform on June 10, 2025. It supports second-by-second interest calculations, ownership transfers, and daily distributions, including weekends and holidays.

I've been connecting the institutional developments behind this, and the implications for these three networks are extremely bullish to me.

Let's start with $XRP.

On September 18, 2025, Franklin Templeton, Ripple, and DBS Bank announced plans to connect sgBENJI tokenized money-market fund shares with RLUSD through DBS Digital Exchange.

Franklin Templeton selected XRP Ledger for sgBENJI because of its speed, efficiency, and low transaction costs.

Imagine an institution holding $10 million in RLUSD. Through the planned arrangement, it could exchange those digital dollars for money-market fund shares that generate income, then move back into RLUSD when it needs liquidity.

The companies are also exploring using those fund shares as collateral for borrowing.

Personally, I believe combining interest-generating investments with stablecoin liquidity and collateral services could make XRPL increasingly valuable to institutional finance.

And the latest development makes me even more bullish.

On October 22, 2026, Franklin Templeton issued approximately $150 million in additional sgBENJI shares on XRP Ledger.

Two issuances of roughly 72.18 million shares each brought the recorded balance to approximately 192.7 million shares, worth around $200 million at $1.039 per share.

That's almost four times the previous recorded value of approximately $50 million, with the shares held in one authorized wallet.

We're talking about substantial tokenized investment fund issuance on XRPL.

Franklin Templeton also launched its XRP ETF, XRPZ, on November 24, 2025, with approximately $363.11 million in net assets reported as of September 15, 2026.

I love seeing both sides of institutional adoption developing: traditional investment exposure to XRP and regulated financial assets being issued on its underlying network.

More institutional accounts, tokenized assets, and settlement activity can generate XRP transaction fees and reserve requirements. XRPL's decentralized exchange also allows XRP to serve as an intermediary asset when liquidity moves between issued currencies.

Now stellar:native has an equally important connection.

Franklin Templeton launched its Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund, FOBXX, on Stellar in April 2021.

It became the first U.S.-registered mutual fund to use a public blockchain as its official system for recording ownership and processing transactions.

On April 30, 2026, Franklin Templeton and the Stellar Development Foundation celebrated BENJI's fifth anniversary.

The fund had more than $650 million in assets on Stellar at that time, while an October 6, 2026, case study reported approximately $605 million.

Its capabilities include peer-to-peer share transfers, second-level interest calculations, daily dividends, and near-instant settlement around the clock.

Then, on August 12, 2026, the SEC's Division of Investment Management issued a no-action letter covering Franklin Templeton's proposed custody arrangements for registered funds holding FOBXX shares.

The arrangements involve Stellar wallets, hourly fund valuations, intraday trading, cash management, and potential securities-lending collateral.

Imagine how significant that could become if more traditional investment funds begin managing their available cash through BENJI.

For stellar:native, growing fund activity means more opportunities for Stellar accounts, asset transfers, transaction fees, and native-token reserves.

And hedera-hashgraph:native is already supporting another major part of this financial transformation.

On June 11, 2026, Archax introduced near-second-by-second cash-flow technology on Hedera, allowing income from tokenized securities to follow ownership changes and be distributed through USDC.

It also supports fractional ownership, continuous coupon payments, and revenue distributions.

Even more interesting, Lloyds Banking Group, Aberdeen Investments, and Archax completed a UK-first transaction on July 14, 2025, using tokenized money-market fund units and UK government bonds as collateral for foreign exchange trades on Hedera.

Archax's ecosystem also includes tokenized fund exposure involving State Street, Fidelity International, Legal & General Investment Management, and BlackRock, alongside Aberdeen Investments.

Its September 2025 pooled-token development allows multiple money-market investments to be represented together.

Hedera reports more than 100 tokenized assets and over $300 million in tokenized asset value through Archax.

Every additional asset issuance, transfer, income distribution, and smart-contract operation can create more HBAR-denominated network activity. Hedera's fees are priced in dollars and paid through HBAR, which also supports network staking.

And look at Franklin Templeton's other developments.

On February 11, 2026, Franklin Templeton and Binance launched a live program allowing eligible institutions to use tokenized money-market fund shares as trading collateral while those assets remain in off-exchange custody.

On June 2, Franklin Templeton partnered with MoonPay Trade to connect stablecoins with tokenized money-market investments for treasury management, portfolio rebalancing, liquidity, and collateral applications.

Now connect everything.

Financial institutions are developing ways to earn income on capital, transfer investments, access stablecoin liquidity, and use eligible securities as collateral through increasingly connected systems.

I believe this could become a major institutional growth driver through 2027.

For XRP, I'm watching more sgBENJI issuance, RLUSD settlement, institutional liquidity, and collateral applications.

For XLM, I'm watching additional BENJI adoption, fund accounts, and institutional cash-management activity.

For HBAR, I'm watching the expansion of Archax's tokenized securities, automated income payments, and institutional collateral services.

The numbers I'll follow most closely are tokenized fund assets, active institutional accounts, trading and collateral transactions, stablecoin settlement volumes, and actual native-token usage.

I've remained bullish on these networks because I believe institutions will increasingly value this kind of financial infrastructure.

Seeing Franklin Templeton, Ripple, DBS, Stellar, Archax, Hedera, Lloyds, Aberdeen, Binance, and MoonPay building different parts of this future makes my conviction even stronger.

The more I research what institutions are actually developing, the more bullish I become on $XRP, stellar:native, and hedera-hashgraph:native for the long term.

I haven't seen anyone explain just how BIG this latest $XRP news is. 

So I'm going to break it down for you.

Aviva Investors just launched a £50 million tokenized share class of its Sterling Liquidity Fund on XRP Ledger.

And the fund behind it manages £22 BILLION!

We're talking about Aviva's largest investment fund, established back in 2002. Its parent investment business manages approximately £273 billion.

The company already launched its USD liquidity fund share class on XRPL in July. With the new GBP offering, more than £86 million ($116 million) has been invested across both tokenized products.

Now consider the potential scale.

If just 5% of that £22 billion Sterling fund were represented through tokenized shares, we're talking about £1.1 billion. At 10%, that's £2.2 billion.

Those are my expansion scenarios, and Aviva CEO Mark Versey has already expressed interest in exploring more opportunities with Ripple.

But I've found something even more interesting.

Ripple invested in Licuido and ZILO in August.

Licuido is helping Aviva launch these products and is developing infrastructure for tokenized asset trading and collateral. ZILO specializes in fund recordkeeping.

Aviva also recently discussed how tokenized money-market funds could be used as collateral.

And Ripple already has a similar initiative with Franklin Templeton and DBS, involving sgBENJI, RLUSD, and potential financing against tokenized fund shares.

Look at the institutional connections.

BNY safeguards Aviva's underlying fund assets and is also the primary reserve custodian for RLUSD.

Komainu, which supports the Aviva launch, was founded through relationships involving Nomura, Ledger, and CoinShares.

And October 26 brought three major developments: Aviva's Sterling fund launch, final OCC approval for Ripple National Trust Bank, and Ripple Treasury's expanded corporate cash-management services.

Ripple Prime also participates in a DTCC tokenization working group alongside institutions such as BlackRock, JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Franklin Templeton.

DTCC, Citi, and SWIFT have separately been researching how traditional securities and digital financial infrastructure can work together.

Here's my biggest bullish prediction for $XRP.

As more GBP and USD financial products arrive on XRPL, institutions could eventually need deeper cross-currency liquidity.

XRP can serve as an intermediary asset through XRPL's auto-bridging technology. More accounts and transactions also create XRP reserve and fee activity.

I believe the long-term opportunity is much bigger than the initial £50 million.

Ripple is bringing investment funds, digital dollars, custody, collateral, and corporate treasury infrastructure into an expanding institutional ecosystem.

I'm extremely bullish on where this could take $XRP through 2027.

This is one of the biggest reasons I remain extremely bullish on $XRP and $HBAR. 

Have you watched this?

At DC Fintech Week 2026, Jerome Johnson from Amazon Web Services explained how quantum computing is moving toward real-world applications, and I believe the implications for the future financial system are enormous.

Quantum computers use qubits to solve certain complex problems differently from traditional computers. 

Johnson expects quantum and classical computers to work together, giving financial institutions more advanced ways to manage investments, liquidity, and risk.

And major banks are already experimenting with it.

HSBC and IBM achieved up to a 34% improvement in predicting European corporate bond trade outcomes using quantum-classical computing.

JPMorganChase is also working with OQC and AMD on a Quantum-AI Data Centre in London, researching portfolio optimization and quantum machine learning.

Now imagine banks using these technologies to make financial decisions while blockchain networks handle the movement, ownership, and settlement of assets.

And those assets will need strong security for decades.

Ripple is already preparing XRP Ledger for that future.

On April 20, 2026, Ripple announced its post-quantum security roadmap, targeting 2028 for native quantum-resistant signatures.

It's also working with Project Eleven on validator security, institutional custody, wallets, and transaction signing.

The XLS-295 proposal covers ML-DSA-44 signatures, based on NIST's post-quantum standard, with experimental work on XRPL AlphaNet.

XRPL also supports key rotation, allowing institutions to update account credentials while keeping their existing accounts.

I believe this will become increasingly valuable as banks move more financial assets onto blockchain infrastructure.

Look at Ripple's institutional developments.

Franklin Templeton and DBS are working with Ripple on trading sgBENJI tokenized money-market fund shares against RLUSD on XRPL, with plans to explore collateral-based financing.

Ripple Prime has also expanded 24/7 institutional market access through perpetual swaps across more than 100 reference markets, with Virtu among its institutional clients.

These are separate financial services, but they show how widely Ripple is expanding its institutional business.

And $HBAR has another major advantage in its security architecture.

Hedera already uses SHA-384 hashing and AES-256 encryption, providing important cryptographic foundations for its post-quantum transition.

Leemon Baird, Rohit Sinha, and Ed Marquez outlined plans for new quantum-resistant signatures, hybrid security, and account-key upgrades, with post-quantum user keys targeted for 2027.

IBM and Google are also members of Hedera's Governing Council, bringing major technology organizations into its governance.

Meanwhile, Lloyds Banking Group, Aberdeen Investments, and Archax have demonstrated tokenized collateral transactions on Hedera.

Archax has also introduced near-second-by-second income distributions using USDC.

Even the Bank for International Settlements, European central banks, SWIFT, and Nexi-Colt have tested quantum-resistant payment infrastructure through Project Leap.

And the NSA is introducing new post-quantum requirements beginning in 2027, with certain legacy systems targeted for phaseout by 2030.

I believe long-term financial security will become increasingly important as institutional blockchain adoption grows.

More activity on XRPL can create demand for XRP through reserves, transaction fees, and liquidity services. On Hedera, token transfers, smart contracts, collateral, and payments generate HBAR-denominated network usage.

I've remained bullish on $XRP and $HBAR because I believe their technology has a serious future in institutional finance. 

These developments strengthen that conviction even more.

Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
